> 🔁 **Systemic pattern — now three confirmed instances. Check for it before trusting any validator
> or guard in this repo.**
> *An optional constructor dependency defaults to an inert value; the tests pass it explicitly and
> prove the logic; every production site omits it, so the feature is silently dead.*
> 1. **BP-29** — `PredicateCompiler`'s `blueprintRegistry` → conditional breakpoints never fired. **Fixed.**
> 2. **BP-61** — `HsmValidator`'s `isStatefulSubtree` + `sharedScopeKeys` → both HSM concurrency rules
>    never fire. **Open.**
> 3. **BP-30/BP-31** — the same blind spot is *why* BP-31 was mis-scoped: it credited HSM with a guard
>    that has never actually run.
> A green test suite is not evidence that a guard is wired. Grep the production construction sites.

> (BP-72) · pass parameters · wire the return (BP-71) · N outputs (BP-73) · call another blueprint's
> function (`CallPeerBlueprint` + BP-66). **Missing, now tracked:** collapse-a-selection into a
> function (**BP-74**) · a function has no palette entry and cannot be dragged (**BP-75**) ·
> Go-to-Definition/Expand can never enable (**BP-76**) · the Macros "+" button is dead (**BP-77**) ·
> macros as a capability (**BP-78** — design **closed** 2026-08-07 by
> [Q25](Architect_Question_25_Macros.md); building as **BP-79…BP-83**) ·
> function-local variables (**BP-57**, already open).
> ⚠ **Two of these had been sitting in "Out of scope" on a false premise** — see that section. Fifth
> and sixth overturned "nothing exists" claim, same root cause every time: `Hrot/` searched, `FDP/`
> not.
> ⭐ **The finding that reframes macros:** **BP1650** forbids latent nodes in any called function
> graph, because a function is a plain `static` method and the latent cursor/resume machinery exists
> only for the top-level graph. A macro **inlines** ⇒ it is the **only** construct that can factor out
> a reusable *latent* sequence. That, not Unreal parity, is the argument.

> ✅ **Batch 18 shipped (2026-08-06) — [BP-73](Blueprint_Issues_Detail.md#bp-73): Function graphs may
> declare N outputs (Unreal parity).** Closes **Q24-D**, the one sub-question BP-71 left open.
> **Carrier: `ValueTuple`**, decided on evidence rather than taste —
> `CSharpEmitter.IsReferencableStateFieldType:330` treats a `_`-prefixed synthesized type as **not
> referencable** outside the generated class and excludes it from the debug map, so the
> `_FuncOut_{Name}` struct that the *"easier to name in the watch panel"* argument favoured would in
> fact be **invisible to the watch**.
> ⚡ **The finding that shrank the slice:** the carrier needs **no `IrTypeRef` representation at all**.
> Temps emit as `var __tN = …`, so C# infers it; only the three method-**declaration** sites need a
> composed type string, and all three already read `graph.Outputs` — one shared `CSharpReturnType`
> covers them. N-output never enters the type system, which is why ~330 lines was enough.
> `IrOp_MakeTuple` packs in a statement *before* the return, so **`IrTerm_Return` keeps its single
> `IrValue`** and every consumer of it (block emitters, debug map, breakpoint anchoring) is untouched.
> `IrOp_TupleField` reads elements **positionally** (`ItemN`), which is also why the emitted tuple is
> **unnamed**: named elements inherit the `ItemN` positional-collision rule and buy nothing the emit
> uses. Library dispatch writes outputs **sequentially** with an `__oo` advance — blitting the tuple
> would embed the ValueTuple's CLR padding while the reader walks fields by `Unsafe.SizeOf<T>`, and for
> `(bool, float)` those disagree: a wrong-**VALUES** bug, not a compile error.
> ⚠ **Retiring a gate is never one edit.** BP1656 said *"not supported yet — see BP-73"*, so shipping
> BP-73 had to touch the validator, **BP-71's test asserting the gate fires** (inverted rather than
> deleted, so the transition stays visible), and the diagnostic-**coverage ratchet**, whose
> not-emitted list is now documented to cover *retired* as well as *reserved* codes. The code stays in
> `DiagnosticCodes` so the number is never reused.
> ⚠ **Trap #9 again, twice.** 13 tests, and reverting the source confirms **9 of 12 go red** — the 3
> that stay green are exactly the additivity guards, which must not move. One test compiles through
> **Roslyn**, the only check that proves the emit is *valid* C# (`Compile(...).Succeeded` does **not**
> run it), and it earned its place immediately by catching a fixture bug: a `System.Single` literal
> authored as `1.5` emits a C# **double**, because `ValueJson` is emitted **verbatim** and float
> literals need the `f` suffix. A second test was tightened after review — it asserted inside
> `if (src is not null)` and so could pass vacuously.
> All eight gates green (blueprints **2854/0**, 10 skipped).

> ✅ **Batch 17 shipped (2026-08-06) — [BP-69](Blueprint_Issues_Detail.md#bp-69) 🔴, and the general
> unwired-pin hardening it forced.** `CallCustomEventNode.EventId` accepts a GUID or a bare Name;
> `Stage5.FindCustomEventIndex`, Stage 2's `V_ValueNodeReferences`/`V_CustomEventHandlers` and BP-12b's
> rename all honour both, but **both pin projections** bailed on `!Guid.TryParse`. Both now resolve
> through a shared `ResolveCustomEventDecl` mirroring `FindCustomEventIndex`.
> ⚠ **This was filed `WIRING`/"three lines each" and that estimate was wrong** — not in size, in
> *consequence*. Creating the argument pins exposed the next defect immediately: an **unwired**
> argument pin went through `ResolveDataPin`'s dummy path, which allocates an `IrValue` with **no
> producing statement**, and a value is only declared in the generated C# by the statement that
> produces it. The emit became `Event_X(..., __t0, __t1)` with no `var __t0` anywhere — **CS7036
> traded for CS0103**, both Roslyn errors that no BP diagnostic explains. Shipping that would have
> been a lateral move, so `ResolveDataPin` now emits a typed `default(T)` `IrOp_Const`, hardening
> **all ~20 `ResolveDataPin` call sites** rather than only the return terminator
> [BP-71](Blueprint_Issues_Detail.md#bp-71) covered.
> ⚠ **Trap #9 struck this batch's own tests.** The first end-to-end test **passed against the bug**:
> its caller graph had no exec links, so no call site was emitted at all, and
> `IndexOf("Event_OnDamaged(")` matched the method **declaration** rather than the invocation. It was
> caught only by *reverting the fix to confirm the tests went red* — they didn't. **Reverting to watch
> a test fail is now the standard step, not an optional one.** The test asserts on trimmed invocation
> lines and pins the exact argument-less text the defect produced; 4 of the 7 new tests go red on
> revert, verified.
> All eight gates green (blueprints **2842/0**, 10 skipped; breakpoints 130; NodeEdit core 208 + UI
> 131; AiShared 1204; BTree editor 612; generators 189; build 0 errors).

> package **Q23 A2+B2+C2+D1** (self-researched round, recorded in

> **A2:** a switch retargets `BlueprintGraphModel` + `BlueprintCommandSink` **in place** — the

> Event-graph open preference is dead (it moved the canvas whenever an asset gained an Event graph);

> My Blueprint (Graphs/Functions sections split Unreal-style; custom events navigate to their body);

> ✅ **Batch 14 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-19 + BP-20: minimap and jump-to-issue.**

> ✅ **Batch 13 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-17 + BP-18: node titles and body collapse.**
> Both were the same shape: the canvas already honoured the feature (`NodeRenderer` draws a subtitle
> and a collapsed node), but `BlueprintNodeModel` hardcoded `Subtitle => null` / `IsCollapsed =>
> false` and nothing could change either. `SetNodeCollapsed` even existed as a command — **the sink
> had no case, so it hit the `default:` that returns success**, the third instance of that trap
> after BP-60 and BP-68.
> ⚠ A renamed node keeps its **generated title as the subtitle**, and **blank clears the override**
> rather than storing an empty header. Both new `NodeMetadata` fields are omitted from JSON at their
> defaults, so existing assets round-trip byte-identically.

> ✅ **Batch 12 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-13: align / distribute / straighten.**
> Nine declared command ids, zero implementations, all of them a batch move — so all nine reduce to
> `CommandBuilder.MoveNodes` and each is one undo entry for free. Registered in NodeEdit itself: no
> asset knowledge is involved, unlike BP-23a/BP-60.
> ⚠ Alignment works on node **bounds**, not origins (right/centre by the top-left corner leaves
> different-width nodes ragged); distribute equalises **edge** gaps and holds the extremes still, so
> it is idempotent; straighten **anchors on the first selected node** rather than averaging, so the
> designer keeps control and a second invocation changes nothing. An alignment that would move
> nothing records nothing — it must not cost a Ctrl+Z.

> ✅ **Batch 11 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-12b: My Blueprint items can be renamed, duplicated, deleted.**
> The context menu has always invoked all three; nothing ever registered them. Works for variables
> and custom events, undoable on the same stack as everything else.
> ⚠ **Renaming a custom event also renames its paired `Event` graph and rewrites name-keyed
> `CallCustomEvent` references** — the compiler emits `Event_{Name}` from the *graph*, and Stage5
> accepts a bare name, so renaming the declaration alone would be a silent BP1407/BP1403.
> ⚠ **Deleting a declaration leaves its nodes in place.** Dangling is recoverable and the compiler
> names it; silently deleting a designer's wired-up nodes is not.

> ✅ **Batch 10 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-23a: copy / cut / paste / duplicate.**
> Registered host-side for the same reason as BP-60: a clipboard entry is a list of asset `Node`s.
> `Node` is already `[JsonPolymorphic]`, so the round-trip is free; paste re-mints node **and pin**
> GUIDs, remaps the links whose *both* ends were copied, and rejects foreign clipboard text.
> ⚠ **Paste ships fully-built nodes through `BlueprintEditCommand`**, never `AddNode` — that path
> re-applies only `ApplyInitialProperties`' 8-of-50 whitelist and would have silently stripped the
> configuration of the other 42 kinds. A test pins exactly that.
> Duplicate deliberately does **not** touch the clipboard. Paste leaves its nodes selected.

> ✅ **Batch 9 shipped (2026-08-05) — BP-60: "Promote to Variable" works.**
> Fixed as a **host command**, not a sink case. `GraphCommand.PromoteToVariable` is one opaque
> command whose new-node id the sink allocates internally, so no caller could write its inverse —
> that is precisely why BP-02 left this site on `Commands.Apply` and why it reached the
> `default:` arm that returns success. Promotion is not one primitive anyway: it is *declare a
> variable* + *place a node* + *link it*. Composing it at the host from commands the sink already
> implements keeps BP-11's invariant (**the sink applies, the stack records**) and makes the whole
> gesture **one undo entry**, because the caller owns every id in it.
> **This lifts BP-02's 15th and last undo bypass.** ⚠ Every test asserts the *effect*; a test on
> `Success` would have passed against the bug.

> ✅ **Batch 8 shipped (2026-08-05) — custom-event authoring: BP-12c + BP-68.**
> "Custom Events +" opens a create modal (name + typed parameters), mirroring `editor.create-variable`
> exactly. This **unblocks BP-07**, whose picker was correct but had nothing it could ever list.
> ⚠ **The dispatcher half was retired, not wired** — the audit's own suggestion; BP-09 had already
> deleted the concept's node kinds and nothing consumes `EventDispatchers`.
> ⚠ **Found while fixing: a declaration is only half a custom event.** The body is an `Event` graph of
> the same name, which the editor cannot create (**BP-24**) — so calling an unhandled event emitted C#
> that did not compile, blaming a method the designer never wrote. New **BP1407/BP1408** make that a
> Stage 2 error naming the graph to add. They fire at **call sites only**, so the new create button
> never produces a broken asset on its own.
> ⚠ **BP-68, found in this batch's own visual check:** the moment an asset *had* a custom event, the
> next gesture — dragging it onto the canvas — exposed that the sink binds nothing for asset-scoped
> dynamic kinds. Fixed for all three of them.

## Area A — Graph editor UX
*Canvas ergonomics. Mostly NodeEdit-core capability the Blueprint host never registers.*
→ [detail](Blueprint_Issues_Detail.md#area-a--graph-editor-ux)

- [x] **[BP-59](Blueprint_Issues_Detail.md#bp-59)** 🔴 · `WIRING` — **Context-menu "Delete Node" is not undoable, but the Del key is.** `CanvasRenderer.cs:758` applies `RemoveNodes` raw; `EditCommands.cs` builds a proper inverse for the same intent. Silent unrecoverable data loss — *found in the verification pass*

Counted **by id** (that is how `Stage5.FindLocalIndex` resolves — id-only, no name fallback, so a node carrying the NAME is not a reference at all) and **across the whole asset** (a node in another graph carrying the id is exactly the dangling case `BP1670` refuses). Undo on **every** gesture (snapshot, never prediction; all graphs, because a BP-24 switch between edit and undo must not silently restore nothing; deep copies, because rename mutates in place), and a no-op gesture records **no** entry (`BP-204`'s degenerate case). ⭐ Rename needed nothing and was **proven** rather than “fixed”: a local resolves by id, so a rename cannot re-target a reference — the exact **opposite** of `BP-225`'s exec pins, where identity IS the name. **Batch 43 — the surface, asked for and skipped twice before:** a sixth **`Local Variables`** section in `BlueprintMyBlueprintModel`, ⭐ the only **graph**-scoped one. ""` — **no literal conversion at all** — and the emitters then wrote `s.{Name} = {DefaultValueCSharp};`. ⇒ a `float` variable with default `0.5` emitted `s.Ratio = 0.5;`, a C# **`double`** literal, and Roslyn refused it with **`CS0664`** naming a generated file rather than the variable. ⛔ **The same `__var_-1` / `BP-228` shape a fourth time: a diagnostic in the wrong language.** ⚠ **Latent, not live:** every shipped default is integral, `false` or absent, which is why it never fired — ⭐ **found Batch 57 the first time a fixture asked for `0.5`**. 🛠 **Fixed Batch 61.** ⭐ **One converter, `DefaultLiteral.TryToCSharp(IrTypeRef, json)`**, called from all three Stage 5 sites (asset declarations, graph locals, custom-event parameters) so a local's literal cannot drift from a variable's: `F`/`D`/`M` for the fractional types, `L`/`UL`/`U` for the wide integrals, range-checked parsing for the narrow ones, and `true`/`false` matched exactly. ⭐⭐ **Refusal, not pass-through** — ➕ **`BP1674`**, reported against the DECLARATION, for anything with no faithful literal (a struct, a vector, a synthesized `__List_…` wrapper, a number that does not fit). ⚠⚠ **The correction the suite made, not reasoning:** a **`0` means "leave it zero-initialised", for EVERY type** — that is the pre-existing contract, because the emitters skipped `"0"` unconditionally. The first draft special-cased only the no-literal-form types and still broke a `bool` output variable carrying `0`; ⛔ three `ListVariable*` families and the `ListVariableDemo` recipe were red before the rule was made uniform. ⭐ **Two second-order fixes fell out:** the emitters' inline `!= "0"` became `DefaultLiteral.IsSkippable` (it must still recognise the lowering passes' hand-written `"0f"`/`"default"`), and a graph local with default `0` now emits `= default` rather than `= 0` — strictly better, since the old form emitted `Vector3 x = 0;` (CS0029) for a struct-typed local. 🔴 **Red first, 12 of 21 fixtures on revert** — ⚠ and the FIRST probe was invalid: `if (true) return …` failed the build with CS0162-as-error, so the run that reported green had used a stale binary. Re-probed with a foldable-proof condition. ⭐ **One fixture goes through REAL Roslyn** (`CompileAndLoad`), because the text-comparison fixtures would otherwise assert that the emitter writes what the emitter writes. ⭐ **`StructureHash` cannot move:** `StructureHashComputation` hashes name·type·offset·size and **not** the default — so the STOP condition was unreachable by construction, stated rather than hoped. **Tier 2 moves by 4 lines across 3 assets** (`100`→`100F` ×2, `-1`→`-1L` ×2); Tier 1 and `persistence-shape.txt` byte-identical *— found Batch 57 while building `S1`'s read-back fixture, fixed Batch 61*

- [x] **BP-349** · `RW-L` — ⛔⛔ **A CYCLE FENCE OVER `FdpAutoSerializer` CANNOT BE DYNAMIC — measured by the test host ABORTING.** 📐 `Q46` §3 tooth ③ names the hazard *(no cycle guard; a back-reference recurses until the stack dies)* and the handoff sanctions *"a depth/size cap."* 🔴 **The first implementation was a size cap checked DURING the write**, on the reasoning that a cycle emits bytes without bound and trips it long before the stack goes. ⛔⛔ **FALSE, and the rail proved it by killing the whole run:** a self-referencing node with a **single reference member** recurses **without writing one byte per level**, so the stack dies first and no cap is ever consulted — ⚠ and a `StackOverflowException` **cannot be caught in .NET**. ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **the fence must be STATIC:** the type graph is walked once per type *(the same members the serializer follows, plus generic arguments)* and a type that can reach itself is **refused before the serializer runs**. ⚠ **Conservative on purpose and reported as such:** a TREE-shaped type is fenced even when the instance in hand is acyclic, because the serializer is compiled per type and an instance check would have to run the dangerous code to find out. ⭐ The size cap survives as a **second, independent** fence for a huge but acyclic value. ⚠ **Tooth ② is railed, not fixed:** `FdpAutoSerializer` skips get-only properties, so a class exposing state only through computed getters serialises to nothing and **never highlights** — ⛔ the serializer is flight-recorder infrastructure and was not widened. 🔴 **Revert-goes-red 4** *— filed and fixed Batch 94, item `94d`*

**and** `AddStateLayoutField` on `Dispatch == Instance`, and `EmitAiPrimitiveRegistration:329` wrote a literal **`StateSize = 0`** with ⛔ **no `StateFields` block whatsoever** — while `EmitInstanceRegistration:413` emitted the full dictionary. ⇒ `BlueprintDefinition.StateFields` and `DebugMap.StateLayout` were **empty for every AiPrimitive asset**; `TryGetField<T>` could not resolve a name, `MarshalFromBytes` was never reached, and the panel would show `—` for every working-state variable of every type. ⭐⭐ **The sharpest part: the reader was already written and shipped.** `BlueprintDebugSession.CaptureAiPrimitiveState` is named for this exact case — it validates `storedHash == def.StructureHash`, then reads `mapIndex?.StateLayout.Fields` **or** `def.StateFields`. ⛔ **Both empty ⇒ it silently read nothing and returned.** ⚠ **A consumer with no producer, green for its entire life because nothing ever asked it for a value** — `BP-240`'s shape one level up: not *"the corpus does not exercise it"* but *"nothing ever produced the input at all."* 📌 **32 shipped assets are `(Parameter, WorkingState)`; this is not a corner.** 🛠 **Fixed Batch 57 (`S1`).** ⭐ **ONE `EmitStateFieldsBlock`, parameterised by struct name** (`State` / `WorkingState` — those names are ABI), so ruling 9 holds: the AiPrimitive half was missing precisely because there was nothing to add it to. ➕ `StateSize`, `AssetId` and `StateClrType` now real. ⚠⚠ **The trap this batch had to see: `FieldLayout` lays an AiPrimitive's state out from `8`, which is NOT a struct offset** — it is where the working state sits inside `Blackboard1024`, past the stored hash — while an Instance's `16` **is** one (`State` opens with a 16-byte `BlueprintLatentCursor`). 🔴 `CaptureAiPrimitiveState` already reads at `8 + OffsetBytes`, so a descriptor carrying the raw `IrField.Offset` would be **off by exactly 8: plausible bytes from the wrong place**. ⛔ The base cannot simply become 0 — it is hashed into `StructureHash` for all 32 — so the rebase lives in the descriptor emitter and is asserted directly. ⭐ **And the debug map now stays SILENT when the baked offsets are guesses** (`!SizeReliable`): it is a compile-time artefact and cannot emit `Marshal.OffsetOf`, ⛔ and both readers **PREFER `StateLayout` over `StateFields`**, so a baked-and-wrong layout would **shadow** the runtime-derived dictionary that is correct. *(Measured: no shipped asset takes the runtime path today ⇒ a no-op on the corpus and a rail for what comes next.)* 📐 **Checked for a second description before adding one:** `GeneratedBlueprintSchemaCatalog` and `LiveBlackboardValueProvider` both describe **`Parameters` only** — the `(Input, Asset)` cell — so ⭐ **`StateFields` is the FIRST description of AiPrimitive working state, not a third.** 🔴 **Revert-goes-red: 4 of 5** (the fifth is the Instance regression guard). ⭐ Gates: `StructureHash` unchanged for all 42, golden **Tier 1 unchanged**, Tier 2 moved for **27 assets, 27 of 27 AiPrimitive, zero Instance**, `persistence-shape.txt` unchanged *— from `DESIGN_Variable_Details_And_Live_Values.md` §4 blocker `B2`, closed Batch 57*

- [x] **HN-007** · `RW-L` 🔴🔴 — ⭐⭐⭐ **THE PANEL READ PATH WAS DEAD, AND EVERY SUITE WAS GREEN OVER IT.** 📐 `EditorSubsystem.Update` ran `PanelSnapshot.ClearCaptured()` and then `_debugApiJobQueue.DrainAll()` **on the very next line** ⇒ every `GET /panels` served through that queue executed **one statement after the captured set was emptied and before anything refilled it** *(the gizmo feed publishes later in `Update`; every panel publishes in `DrawUI`, later still)*. ⇒ ⛔⛔ **`captured` was STRUCTURALLY ALWAYS EMPTY for every out-of-band reader, and `GET /panels/{id}` answered `null` for every panel that exists.** ⭐⭐⭐ **Found BEFORE a single golden was written — every golden in `DESIGN_Regression_Net.md` would have been a golden of NOTHING**, passing forever. ⚠⚠ **`BP-480`'s own comment argued the opposite** — *"CLEAR-THEN-FILL … so a reader between frames always sees a COMPLETE frame"* — ⭐ true of the INTENT and **false of the only reader it names**: the HTTP reader does not run between frames, it runs INSIDE this one. 📌 **The same blind spot `BP-480` had already declared** *("caught by tracing the call order, not by a rail — no rail spans `Update` and `DrawUI`")*, one step further along. ⭐ Fix: **drain BEFORE clear** ⇒ the reader sees the previous COMPLETE frame, which is exactly what §6's capture protocol already assumed. 📐 **Measured pre-existing, twice**: `PanelSnapshotTests.A_panels_model_can_be_read_and_a_field_asserted` fails identically at the dispatch sha **and** at `b7a92ddb8`, the commit before the perspective rename merged ⇒ ⛔ **older than that batch.** ⚠ The cost, stated: a reader sees a capture one frame old — ⛔ reading a half-built frame is worse, and reading an EMPTY one is what we had *— found by baselining the harness before writing any golden*

## Area K — Panel observability

*⭐⭐ **The `PanelSnapshot` programme** — every panel builds a whole view-model, renders only from it, and
dumps it to a per-frame snapshot tests and MCP read. ⭐ Ids are **`BP-`** *(this is the UI lane's own work,
not a third lane)*, so these rows **do** move the counts table.*
→ design: [DESIGN_UI_Observability_Snapshot.md](../DESIGN_UI_Observability_Snapshot.md) ·
  umbrella: [DESIGN_Headless_Testability.md](../DESIGN_Headless_Testability.md)

- [x] **BP-453** · `RW-M` — ⭐⭐⭐ **`U1a`: `IPanelViewModel` + `PanelDump` + `PanelSnapshot` exist, in `Fdp.Diagnostics.Contracts`.** 📄 §APIs. ⭐ **The home was CONFIRMED, not assumed** *(the handoff asked)*: 📐 every Hrot editor panel assembly reaches that assembly **transitively** — `Hrot.Blueprints.Editor` → `Fdp.Toolkits` → it, `Hrot.Editor.AiShared` → `Fdp.Presentation` → `Fdp.Toolkits` → it ⇒ ⭐ **zero new ProjectReferences.** ⚠ **One limit, stated rather than discovered later:** the `FDP/ExtDeps/NodeEdit` tree references **nothing** from FDP, so a NodeEditor-owned panel cannot see this contract and would need a host-side shim — ⛔ inverting that layering is not on the table. ⭐ Open question ① resolved to the design's own lean: `PanelDump.Of(this)`, STJ over the VM, camelCase, with a VM free to hand-write a `JsonNode` *— built `U-obs-1`*
- [x] **BP-454** · `RW-M` — ⭐⭐⭐ **`U1b`: the opt-in registry is TWO SETS, because one cannot say what the design asks.** 📄 §APIs lists a single `RegisteredPanels`; ⛔ but §"MCP read surface" **requires both halves** — *"the panel ids captured this frame, **and** which panels are instrumented at all"*. ⇒ ⭐ `RegisteredPanels` *(instrumented)* + `CapturedPanels` *(actually dumped)*. ⭐⭐ **And `DeclareInstrumented` is called at CONSTRUCTION, always, ungated by `CaptureEnabled`** — 📐 a panel whose window nobody opens **never draws**, so declaring-by-drawing would make it indistinguishable from a panel nobody converted ⇒ 📌 **the exact false green the opt-in registry exists to prevent.** Probed: moving the call into the draw reddens 2 rails *— built `U-obs-1`*
- [x] **BP-455** · `RW-H` — ⛔⛔⛔ **`U1c`/`U1d`: TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN, both measured, both load-bearing.** ⭐ **① CAPTURE HAPPENS BEFORE THE RENDER GUARD** — §Example orders it build→render→capture, but the pilot's draw opens `if (ImGui.GetCurrentContext() == IntPtr.Zero) return;` ⇒ capturing after it makes the dump **depend on a live GPU context** and ⛔ **a headless run observes NOTHING**, defeating `DESIGN_Headless_Testability.md`, the reason this programme exists. 📐 **Probed: moving the capture back reddens 4 of 6 pilot rails.** ⭐⭐ **② THE PANEL ID IS A DECLARED LITERAL, NOT A WINDOW-MANAGER ID** — 🔴 **the design contradicts itself**: §"Perf & correctness" says *"use the window-manager registration id"*, §Example's payload says `"panelId": "entity-blueprints"`. 📐 §Example wins on two measurements: **(a)** `BlueprintEditorWindowBase` declares **`Title` and nothing else** — there is no id to use; **(b)** where ids exist they are **perspective-suffixed** *(`ai_runtime_inspector_btree`)* to be unique per dock slot ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **a window id is unique by construction, a panel id must be STABLE by construction — opposite requirements**, and using one would give the same logical panel a different key per host, which is precisely what conformance diffs by. 📄 Both folded into the design's AS-BUILT section; the rule lives in `PanelIds`' header *— built `U-obs-1`*

- [x] **CE-036** · `RW-S` ✅ ⭐ — **all three skips removed; 5/5 green, 0 skipped** *(was 2 pass + 3 skipped)*. ⭐⭐ **The skip REASON was the misleading part:** *"Requires CycloneDDS"* reads as *"this environment has no DDS"* — in an assembly whose other tests boot a real CycloneDDS domain and pass. 📐 **The real cause is arithmetic:** CycloneDDS derives its UDP ports as `7400 + 250 × domainId + …`, so `domainId = 250` asks for port **69900**, which does not exist ⇒ ⛔ the harness could never have come up on 250 **on any machine, with or without DDS installed**. ⭐ The usable ceiling is ≈ `(65535 − 7400) / 250 ≈ 232`; changed to **200**, clear of both the ceiling and the auto-counter *(`DomainIdBase = 100`)*. 📌 `R-131`: the fix is the domain id, not a filter
- [x] **CE-030** · `RW-S` ✅ ⚠ — **three `CgfLogicPackTests` had been RED since `2026-08-19` and nobody read them** *(`R-131`)*. 📐 They assert a hard-coded `SimulationSystems.Count == 18`; the real count is **19** because **Batch 94b** *(this same lane)* added `BehaviorFrameSystem` to `CognitiveRuntimeModule` *(`:57`)*, which flows into the pack. ⭐ Counts corrected to 19 / 21 with a note naming the cause, so the next drift is traceable. ⚠ **Found only because a new rail in the same suite went red and forced an attribution pass** — ⛔ the reds were being carried as *"the known order flake"*, and three of them were not: they failed **3/9 in isolation**, deterministically

## Area M — MCP authoring surface

*⭐⭐ **`AQ56`'s partition** — ids are **`MA-`**, never `BP-`/`HN-`/`MX-`/`TM-`/`ST-`/`CE-`, so the lanes
cannot collide by construction. ⚠ **`scripts/tracker-counts.py` only counts rows naming a `BP-` id**, so
nothing here moves the counts table.*
→ design: [DESIGN_Mcp_Authoring.md](../DESIGN_Mcp_Authoring.md) *(**§10 is the AS-BUILT**)* ·
  decision trail: [Architect_Question_56_Mcp_Authoring_Surface.md](Architect_Question_56_Mcp_Authoring_Surface.md) *(resolved)*

- [x] **MA-001** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **`GET /assets/{id}/graph` — the in-memory-faithful read, and it projects `IGraphModel`.** ⛔⛔ **A DEVIATION from design §3, argued:** §3 named `BlueprintClipboard` as *"the closer analog to reuse"*; 📐 measured, the clipboard round-trips `Hrot.Blueprints.Core.Assets.Node` — the **ASSET** model, Blueprint-only, whose own header says the vendored NodeEdit tree *"knows nothing about"* it — and **it carries no `PinId` at all**, so it cannot express the id space `GraphCommand` edits by. ⭐⭐ `InMemoryGraphSerializer` projects **`IGraphModel`/`INodeModel`/`IPinModel`/`ILinkModel`** instead: those expose exactly the `NodeId`/`PinId`/`LinkId` the commands take ⇒ read and edit share one id space **by construction**, ⛔ not by care. ⭐⭐⭐ **And it is HOST-AGNOSTIC — one serializer covers BTree, HSM and Blueprint** where a clipboard-shaped one would have been three. ⚠ §3's RULE *(two id spaces; expose the in-memory ids)* is CORRECT and load-bearing; only its named analog was wrong — design §3 now carries the supersession box
- [x] **MA-002** · `RW-M` ✅ — **the four edit routes, all through the SAME path human editing uses.** `POST /assets/{id}/graph/{nodes,links,params,remove}` → `CommandBuilder` → ⭐⭐ **`GraphView.Execute(fwd, inv, label)`** — ⛔ **not `IGraphCommandSink.Apply` directly**, which is what `AuthoringPath` does in tests and which would SKIP the undo stack. ⇒ an MCP edit is undoable exactly like a human one *(`Q56-A`: "MCP edits ARE human edits over the wire")*. ⭐ add-node RETURNS its guid — the half of `Q56-D` that makes determinism a non-problem. ⚠ **Two shape changes from §5's diagram, both measured:** `CommandBuilder` has **no** `SetNodeProperty` builder and `INodeModel` exposes no property bag ⇒ an inverse could not be built, so **params became a PIN DEFAULT** *(`SetPinDefault`, the one edit whose inverse the model can produce)*; and **remove invokes `editor.delete-selection`** rather than building `RemoveNodes` — ⭐ that command already handles the IMPLICITLY deleted incident links, the reroutes, the attachments, and an inverse whose steps are **reversed** so nodes are restored before the links referencing them. ⛔ A hand-rolled removal gets the last of those wrong SILENTLY: undo appears to work
- [x] **MA-003** · `RW-S` ✅ 🔴🔴 — **CGF's SAVE WAS A SILENT NO-OP AFTER ANY EDIT, and this batch found it.** 📐 Measured: `SaveAllAiDocumentsCommand.Execute` **skips** a document whose `IsDirty` is false, and `AiDocument.MarkDirty` had **exactly ONE production caller in the repo** — the EDITOR's `DocumentOpened` factory *(`EditorSubsystem:4016`)*, which subscribes `doc.Asset.Changed` ⛔ **and only when a regeneration scheduler exists**. ⚠⚠ **CGF's factory never subscribed at all** *(`CE-015` built the factories; the dirty subscription was not among them)* ⇒ ⛔ **CGF could edit a graph and then write NOTHING while reporting success** — `CE-020`'s save was reachable and inert. ⭐ Fixed by adding the subscription to `CgfSubsystem`'s `DocumentOpened`, trimmed to what this host has *(no scheduler — CGF regenerates nothing; the reload compiles from the in-memory asset)*. 📌 **The silent-default shape verbatim: the editor HAD the wiring and CGF did not, and nothing compared them**
- [x] **MA-004** · `RW-S` ✅ ⚠ — ⭐⭐ **`GET /assets/{id}/graph/catalog` — A ROUTE THE DESIGN DID NOT LIST, and building the edit routes is what proved it necessary.** 📐 `add_graph_node` takes a `kind` **string**, and the host sink answers an unknown kind by **building nothing while reporting success** *(`AuthoringPath.AddNode`'s own error message documents exactly that)*. ⇒ ⛔ without a discovery route the agent must GUESS a kind id, and a wrong guess is a silent no-op — 📌 the *"advertised but unreachable"* shape `CE-009` §4c caught. ⭐ `INodeCatalog` already hangs off `GraphView`, so this is a projection, ⛔ not a new registry. ⭐⭐ **And the add-node route now RE-READS the model** *(`FindNode(newId)`)* and 400s if the sink built nothing — ⛔ rather than handing back a guid that addresses nothing. Folded into design §10.2
- [x] **MA-005** · `RW-S` ✅ — **`POST /assets` create, through the host's OWN New-Asset path.** ⭐⭐ The dialog callback's body was **EXTRACTED** into `CreateAssetCore` and both surfaces now run the same lines *(ruling 9)* — ⛔ not a second create for MCP: 📐 that body is **four host-composition facts** a duplicate would get wrong *(Blueprint is mint-only and needs its file written at `_bpRootDir` — `BUG-A6`, the SOURCE dir the contributor scans, not `bin/`; `RefreshFromAssembly` refreshes only the assembly contributors; the JSON contributors must be refreshed SEPARATELY per kind; only then does `FindByAssetId` succeed)*. ⭐ Reached by an `AttachAssetAuthoring(delegate)` seam, the same argument slice 3 made for save/reload. ⚠ **It returns the minted id ONLY once the catalog resolves it** — ⛔ returning it earlier would hand back an id `GET /assets` cannot address
- [x] **MA-006** · `RW-S` ✅ — **`DELETE /entities/{networkId}` — scenario authoring's ONE missing verb.** ⛔ **Design §7 ④ asked to *"extend `/entities/*` for the gaps (place/configure/assign)"*; 📐 measured, all three already existed**: place = `POST /entities/spawn` *(it takes a transform)*, configure = `/attribute` + `/component`, assign = `/attach-blueprint`. ⭐⭐ **Delete had no route at all** ⇒ that is the whole item. It publishes the same `DestroyEntityCommand` CGF's canvas delete and the cluster's `DeleteEntityRequestSystem` publish. ⚠ **Queued like spawn** — ELM teardown runs on a later tick, and the payload says so rather than implying synchrony
- [x] **MA-007** · `RW-S` ✅ — **validation is the HOST's, at the level it actually exists.** ⭐⭐⭐ `add_graph_link` consults **`ILinkValidator`** — the same check the canvas runs while dragging a wire — and a refusal is a **400 carrying the host's own reason text**, ⛔ not a server error: refusing an illegal wire is a legitimate answer. ⚠ Design item ⑤ also named the `IAssetValidator` set; ⛔ **not wired here**, because those validate a whole asset at save/authoring-window time and this surface validates a single edit — filed `MA-008`
- [x] **MA-008** · `RW-S` ✅ — **the MCP surface: 8 `RouteDoc`s + 8 handlers, gated.** 📐 `gen:catalog` **74 → 82 tools**, `gen:skill` regenerated, `test-catalog` **657 / 0** *(it asserts `src/index.mjs` registers a handler for every catalogued tool — 📌 `CE-009` §4c caught six advertised-but-unreachable tools that way)*. ⭐ `CapabilityManifest` needed **no edit**: it is PREFIX-derived and `/assets*` is already `EditorAuthoring` — 📌 `R-133` holding, the manifest measured rather than declared. ⚠ `DELETE /entities/{id}` classifies as `WorldRead` like every other `/entities/*` write *(`spawn`, `command`, `attribute`)*; ⛔ not changed here, because special-casing delete would make the table inconsistent — flagged for whoever revisits write-capability granularity
- [ ] **MA-009** · `RW-S` ⚠ — ⭐ **the per-edit `MarkEdited` guard is NOT rail-covered, and revert probe B is why that is stated rather than assumed.** 📐 With the call commented out the create/edit/save rail stayed **GREEN**, because on the EDITOR the `Asset.Changed` subscription already marks the document. ⇒ ⛔ **the guard is redundant on a correctly-wired host — which is exactly what it defends against**: the subscription is per-host COMPOSITION, which a host can forget and CGF did for three slices *(`MA-003`)*. ⚠ Pinning it needs a host lacking the subscription, and the one that lacked it now has it. ⭐ Filed rather than deleted: deleting it would re-arm `MA-003`'s failure mode for the next host
- [ ] **MA-010** · `RW-M` ⚠ 🔴 — ⭐⭐ **the COMMITTED asset files and what the editor WRITES differ in shape, so any save through the editor dirties the tree.** 📐 Measured the hard way: the first cut of the headline rail edited and saved `ComponentCollectionDemo.bp.json` and `git status` came back with **372 deleted lines**. ⚠ **Not a defect this batch introduced** — `SaveActiveBlueprintCommand` strips the projected pins and rewrites link endpoints to deterministic name-derived ids *(design §3; `AQ10` rehydration reverses it on load)*, so the fatter committed file is simply an older/hand-authored shape. ⛔ Slice 3's rail never noticed because it saved a CLEAN document, which is a no-op. ⇒ ⭐ **the rails are split**: the EDIT half never saves *(it removes what it added and reloads)*, and the SAVE half runs on an asset the rail CREATES in a sentinel folder it deletes. ⚠ Filed because *"the committed assets are not in the shape the editor writes"* is a real question for whoever owns asset persistence — ⛔ out of scope here

- [x] **MA-011** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **the read is COMPLETE: attachments · regions · reroutes.** 📄 design §11.3 / §15.1. `InMemoryGraphSerializer` now emits the **attachment stack per node AND asset-level** *(both, deliberately: "what decorates THIS node" and "what attachments exist at all" are different questions, and a coverage rail needs the second)*, **container regions with each child's `regionIndex`** *(the only way to tell "moved between regions" from "moved on the canvas")*, **reroute waypoints**, link style, and the collapsed/advanced flags. ⭐⭐⭐ **Why it had to land FIRST:** the four typed verbs could not express an attachment, so nothing read one back either ⇒ ⛔ an `AddAttachment` over the union route would have been **UNPROVABLE**. 📌 The read and the write must widen TOGETHER, or the wider write is untestable
- [x] **MA-012** · `RW-H` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **THE UNION BACKBONE: `POST /assets/{id}/graph/command` carries all 35 `GraphCommand` variants.** 📄 design §11.2 / §15.4. Applied through **`GraphView.Execute`** *(the undo stack — ⛔ not the sink directly, which is what `AuthoringPath` does in tests and which SKIPS undo)*; **`Batch` is atomic** with its inverses reversed. ⛔⛔ **Hand-written, not `JsonSerializer` polymorphism:** 📐 the variants are positional records over NodeEdit primitives *(`readonly record struct` id wrappers, `Vector2`/`Vector4`, `IReadOnlyDictionary<string,object?>`)* and **`[JsonPolymorphic]` cannot be added — NodeEdit is a VENDORED tree this lane does not own**. ⭐ The explicit reader also lets every failure NAME the offending field. ⚠⚠ **`undoable:false` is REPORTED, never faked** — the refactor ops, `SetNodeProperty`, `SetAttachmentProperty`, `SetRegionProperty` and `RemoveRegion` have no inverse derivable from the READ-ONLY model, and ⛔ **a wrong inverse corrupts the graph on undo, silently**. ⭐ A `Batch` with any un-invertible step is not undoable as a WHOLE: a partial inverse is worse than none
- [x] **MA-013** · `RW-M` ✅ — **discovery EXTENDS the shipped catalog route; ⛔ no parallel `/nodetypes`.** 📄 design §10.2 / §15.3. `GET …/graph/catalog` and the new `GET …/graph/catalog/{kind}` share ONE `DescribeKind` projection *(⛔ the list previously built its own object literal — two projections of one concept drift, and the drift shows up as a caller trusting the wrong one)*. ⚠⚠ **TWO measured limits, stated IN THE PAYLOAD rather than papered over:** ① **the catalog cannot say whether a kind is a CONTAINER** — container-ness is `IContainerNodeModel`, implemented by an INSTANCE, so the kind payload reports `paletteAction`/`attachmentCategory` *(what the catalog DOES know)* and container structure is reported per NODE; ② **`IActionSchemaExporter` is keyed by action FQN, which belongs to a node INSTANCE, not a kind** *(every production caller reads the fqn off the selected node)* ⇒ the route tries the kind id, then a suffix match, and reports which in **`paramsSource`**. ⛔ An empty param list WITHOUT that field would read as *"this kind has no params"* — a different and often false claim. ⚠ `ActionSchemaEntry.DtoFields` is NULLABLE and null ≠ empty: `none:dto-fields-not-reflected` vs `none:not-an-action`
- [x] **MA-014** · `RW-S` ✅ — **`GET /assets/{id}/graph/nodes/{guid}/properties` — the node's CURRENT values joined with its schema**, which is what the Details panel shows. 📄 design §10.2 ③. ⭐ Only INPUT DATA pins: an exec pin has no value and an output's is computed, so listing them would invite a set that must be refused. ⭐ Range/unit/picker metadata comes off the pin's own default descriptor — ⛔ not re-derived. ⇒ with `MA-013` this closes the loop the user asked for: *list kinds → read a kind's schema → add a node → read its properties → set one → save+reload*
- [x] **MA-015** · `RW-M` ✅ ⚠ — **the EDITOR command bus over MCP, at `/editor/commands` — ⛔ NOT `/commands`.** 📄 design §10.7 / §15.2. 🔴 **`GET /commands` has existed since Group F** as `list_commands` *("enumerate publishable FDP event types with field schemas")* and **`send_entity_command` depends on it** ⇒ taking that path would break a shipped tool. ⭐ The prefix is also the honest name. ⭐⭐⭐ **The assertion that matters: a DISABLED command is refused with `409` BEFORE invoking.** 📐 `EditorCommandsImpl` will run a handler whose `IsEnabled` is false — the UI simply never offers it ⇒ ⛔ without the pre-check **MCP would be the one path that can do what the editor greys out**, which is precisely the parity this whole surface exists to preserve. ⭐ The set is resolved **per active document** through a lambda, ⛔ not captured — it is built by the per-kind factory, so a captured instance would pin the API to whichever document was open at composition. ⚠ Ruling 53: no pre-flight, but **every invocation is LOGGED** — the origin-side log is the whole safety net. ⛔ `GlobalActionRegistry` stays out *(int-keyed, no descriptor)*
- [x] **MA-016** · `RW-S` ✅ — **the usage-doc HARVEST, and the one attribute that was missing.** 📄 design §10.6 / §15.7. Params are documented from the **same attributes the Details editor reads** — `EditDisplayName` · `EditRange` · `EditUnit` · `EditReadOnly` · `InlineArrayHint`/`FixedBufferHint` — plus enum values. ⭐⭐⭐ **`EditDocAttribute` is NEW** *(`StructEdit.Core.Attributes`, additive)*: §10.6 measured that the free-text *"how to use"* half lives **only in XML `<summary>` comments** and is in **no** attribute. It is `RouteDoc.Summary` at field granularity. ⛔ **Never a parallel hand-authored doc table** — 📌 that is the rot `RouteDoc` was built to avoid; it goes stale the first time a field is renamed and nothing fails
- [x] **MA-017** · `RW-M` ✅ 🔴🔴 — **A SINK CAN ACCEPT AND BUILD NOTHING — found by the first run of this batch's own rail.** 📐 **Measured `2026-08-25`:** `AddAttachment` on a **Blueprint** returns `GraphCommandResult.Success` with no message and creates **nothing** — attachments are a BTree/HSM concept *(decorators, condition pills)* and `BlueprintCommandSink` has no arm for them. ⇒ ⛔ trusting `Success` hands the agent an `attachmentId` that addresses nothing. ⭐⭐ **Fixed by generalising `MA-004`'s add-node lesson to the WHOLE union: every id a command MINTS must resolve in the model before the route reports success** — so a host that cannot serve a variant SAYS so, naming the variant and why. ⚠ **And a second measurement on the retry:** a BTree needs `hostProperties.paletteKind` to know WHICH decorator to construct *(what `PaletteEntryExecutor` passes when a human picks one)*, and `BTreeCommandSink` refuses `AddComment` outright ⇒ ⭐ the rail now drives each variant on a host that OWNS it, and logs every refusal rather than skipping it
- [x] **MA-018** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **the coverage rails, and the one that makes the union fix PERMANENT.** ⭐⭐⭐ `TheCommandRouteCoversTheWholeUnionTests` is a **UNIT** rail *(~5 ms, no editor)*: it reflects over `GraphCommand`'s nested types and fails when a variant is **neither reachable nor declared unsupported** — and fails the OTHER way on a row naming a variant that no longer exists. 📌 §11.2's whole argument is that *"a hand-picked verb list WILL lag the union"*; ⛔ replacing four hand-picked verbs with **thirty-five hand-written arms** fixes today and re-opens the same decay tomorrow ⇒ ⭐ this rail is what makes it permanent. 📐 Probed by deleting the `AddRegion` row: reddens naming it. ⭐ Plus three T3 rails — the union round-trip *(per host)*, schema coverage over **every** catalogued kind, and the command bus *(discoverable · describable · the 409 parity assertion)*. ⚠ **Doc coverage is MEASURED against a floor, not asserted at 100%**, and the split is deliberate: a schema comes from registries the host must already populate to draw its palette ⇒ a kind it cannot describe is a real defect; ⛔ prose is different — demanding 100% today would redden on a gap this slice **opened the door to closing** rather than one it caused

### ⭐ `AQ57` — **CREATE on a cluster node** *(`2026-08-25`)*
→ design: [Architect_Question_57_Cgf_Authoring_Packaging.md](Architect_Question_57_Cgf_Authoring_Packaging.md) *(**§AS BUILT** carries the UML + the two deviations)*

- [x] **MA-019** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **CGF composes the per-kind `INewAssetService` dictionary, so a CLUSTER NODE can CREATE.** 📐 `create_asset` shipped with `MA-002` and worked ONLY on the editor: the dictionary was a literal behind `Hrot.Editor`, which CGF cannot reference *(ruling 66)*. ⭐⭐ **Measured first, and it is what made the slice cheap:** CGF ALREADY references the three per-kind editor assemblies *(`Hrot.CGF.csproj` 43/52/53)* ⇒ **no reference was added and no registry was built** — `WireAssetCreation` constructs the dict and publishes it, and `ClusterRunner/Program.cs` attaches it at the one composition root that sees both halves *(the third time for that same reference-wall reason)*. ⚠ The four host-composition facts are mirrored deliberately, not by copy-instinct: the Blueprint SOURCE root, the assembly refresh, the per-kind JSON contributor refresh, and only THEN `FindByAssetId` — ⛔ **the id is returned only once the CATALOG resolves it** *(`MA-004`)*
- [x] **MA-020** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **`GET /assets/recipes` + the `describe` seam that was inert.** ⭐⭐⭐ **The route BUILDS NOTHING:** `RecipePickerSource` *(AiShared)* has always projected `AvailableRecipes()` per kind, so this takes the same dictionary the New-Asset picker takes and reports the same projection over HTTP — ⛔ a parallel recipe registry would be ruling 9's duplicate. ⚠⚠ **And it uncovered a silent default:** `RecipePickerSource`'s `describe`/`recipeCategory` seams have existed since it was written, **`RecipeMetadataAdapter.ToShared` had ZERO production callers**, and `NewAssetLauncher` was constructed with neither ⇒ **every recipe rendered with a null description while `BlueprintAsset.EditorMetadata.Recipe` held one** — 📌 the caller HAD the value and did not pass it. ⭐ Now wired for BOTH surfaces from one resolver: 📐 **`17 / 21` recipes carry a description; the revert probe measures `0 / 21`**
- [x] **MA-021** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **`POST /assets` takes an optional `recipe` NAME.** ⛔ **A deviation from `Q57-C`, argued:** taken literally *"reuse the shipped create route"* + *"expose recipe discovery"* are incoherent — the shipped route resolved the kind's **blank template and nothing else**, so every recipe discovery listed would have been **unbuildable**. ⭐ Still not a second create path *(the constraint that mattered)*: `CreateAssetDelegate` gained a parameter. ⭐⭐⭐ **An unmatched name is REFUSED with the names that would have worked** — ⛔ never a silent fall back to blank, which would hand the caller a different asset than it asked for and report success. ⭐ `RecipeByName.Resolve` is SHARED *(AiShared)* because both hosts create and the rule is one rule
- [x] **MA-022** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐ — **CGF wires an `IActionSchemaExporter`**, so `get_node_kind_schema` stops answering `paramsSource: none:no-exporter-wired` on a cluster node *(the one-line follow-up the overnight MCP run filed)*. ⛔ **`Rebuild()` is not optional:** the exporter is born empty and is otherwise refreshed only by `ActionSchemaExporterCatalogWatcher`, which CGF does not wire — ⚠ an un-rebuilt exporter would make every kind report an EMPTY param list, which reads as *"this kind has no params"* rather than *"nothing was reflected"*
- [x] **MA-023** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **the conformance rail, on `--mode all` and nowhere else.** ⭐ A rail on the editor would prove nothing: the editor never had the gap. 📐 Discovery → create BY NAME → the node's catalog gains it → an unknown recipe is refused → `none:no-exporter-wired` does not occur. ⚠ **Discovery and create are asserted TOGETHER, deliberately** — a list of recipes the create route cannot build from is a capability reported and not held, the shape `MA-004` and `MA-017` each caught once. ⭐⭐ **Two revert probes, both red:** un-wire `AttachRecipes` ⇒ 503 naming the missing call; drop the `describe` seam ⇒ `0/21` naming the un-wired state. ⚠ Every id it reads back it then USES, and the anti-vacuity floor guards the exporter claim against an empty sample

## Area M — Axis B: authority-aware entity writes

> ⭐ **New id prefix `AX-`**, in its own area, per the Axis-B handoff *(clear of `MA-`/`CE-`)*.
> 📄 Design: [`DESIGN_Cgf_AxisB_Rotation_Slice.md`](../DESIGN_Cgf_AxisB_Rotation_Slice.md) — ⭐ **read §9
> AS-BUILT first**; it supersedes §1's gate row and §6 ①'s framing.

- [x] **AX-001** · `RW-M` ✅ 🔴🔴 — **`UXI-30`'s STATED PREMISE IS FALSE, and measuring it is what produced a better fix.** ⛔ The design says *"`BinaryInterpreter.Apply` — **no authority gate** … dispatches every record to its handler with no `CanWrite`"*. 📐 **Measured `2026-08-25`: BOTH production installers already gated EVERY handler** — `SimTransformAttributeInstaller` *(4 checks)*, `EntityDataAttributeInstaller` *(2)* — with `if (!ctx.PatchContext.CanWrite<T>()) return;`. ⇒ ⭐ **the binary path WAS authority-gated**, per handler, ⭐⭐ **which is the JSON path's own architecture**: the design's own inventory points at `JsonAttributeCompiler`, whose gate lives in the typed `ValueInvoker<T>` and **not** in the router either. ⇒ ⛔ *"the router has no gate"* was never the defect. ⭐⭐⭐ **The real defect: the gate was PER-INSTALLER and therefore FORGETTABLE** — and this slice adds a THIRD installer, which is exactly when that bites: one omitted line writes an unowned component **silently**. ⇒ built `BinaryInterpreterBuilder.RegisterHandler<TComponent>` — the gate at REGISTRATION — and **migrated both installers onto it, deleting their hand-written checks**, so there is ONE implementation. ⭐ The rail asserts it on a handler that is a bare counter: ⛔ it proves the REGISTRATION gates, not that an author remembered. ✅ **And §6 ①'s *"zero production senders"* independently VERIFIED** — only the receiver reads `AttributeRecords`

## Area N — Test-suite reliability

### ⭐⭐⭐ **The suites were the defect** *(`2026-08-26`, BACKEND lane — handoff `HANDOFF_Test_Suite_Reliability.md`)*
→ durable record: [TESTING_Harness_And_Goldens.md §7](../../TESTING_Harness_And_Goldens.md) *(the leak that read as flakiness · the `LiveInstanceCount` instrument · the three checks before believing a red)*

- [x] **QA-001** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **`HrotNodeContext` had NO ownership contract, so nobody disposed the world.** 📐 Measured: the **four** consumers that receive a world through the record *(`SimHostApp`, `IgApplication`, `CgfSubsystem`, `EyesAndMuscleSubsystem`)* all disposed the KERNEL and **none** disposed the WORLD; the **three** that build their own *(`CgfApplication`, `EditorSubsystem`, `ScenarioSubsystem`)* all dispose it. ⇒ ⛔ **not four independent oversights — one missing contract.** ⭐ The record is now `IDisposable` *(kernel THEN world, idempotent)*; ⚠ `Participant` deliberately excluded — its ownership is genuinely conditional
- [x] **QA-002** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **a harness constructor that throws must not leak a DDS participant.** ⛔ xUnit does **not** call `Dispose` on an instance whose ctor threw, so an OOM'd `HrotRunnerHarness` left its participant **and a live `HostedIdAllocatorServer` poll thread** running for the life of the process
- [x] **QA-003** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **the fault that stops a THREAD must not stop the PROCESS.** `HostedIdAllocatorServer.RunLoop` had no exception handling, so `DdsException: dds_take failed: -3` became an **unhandled exception on a background thread** and killed the whole host — in production, the node; in the suite, the run. ⛔ **Not a swallow** *(`R-131`)*: logged at ERROR, kept on `LastFault`, loop stops — a reader with a bad handle does not recover by being polled again
- [x] **QA-004** · `RW-M` ✅ ⭐⭐⭐ — **`EntityRepository.LiveInstanceCount` / `IsDisposed`, plus an opt-in origin tracker** *(`FDP_TRACK_REPO_LEAKS=1`)*. ⛔ A leaked repository throws nothing, logs nothing and fails no assertion. ⭐⭐ **This is what turned *"something leaks"* into a LINE NUMBER, twice** — the bare count only ever said *"ten of them, somewhere"*
- [x] **QA-005** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐ — **`DataBreakpointManager` owns and now disposes its post-tick snapshot**; the CGF and editor hosts dispose the manager and their pre-tick snapshot. ⚠ Two more whole repositories per node lifetime
- [x] **QA-006** · `RW-M` ✅ 🔴🔴🔴 — **THE DOMINANT TERM, and it was NOT the world.** `ModuleHostKernel.Initialize` builds a `SnapshotPool` with **`warmupCount: 10`** and nothing ever released it ⇒ ⛔ **every node teardown in the PRODUCT leaked TEN `EntityRepository` instances**, each an `int[1_000_000]` free list plus one `NativeChunkTable` per registered component. ⭐ `SnapshotPool` and `OnDemandProvider` now track every repository they create — **pooled OR leased** — and dispose them; the kernel disposes the pool. ⚠ *"Pooling"* and *"ownership"* are not the same thing: a recycler with no end of life is a leak by construction
- [x] **QA-007** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **`FixedString32/64/128` serialised as a JSON OBJECT, not a string.** `DtoDiagnosticMapper` recursed into the wrapper *(its `FixedBufferAttribute` arm only fires for a fixed buffer that is a FIELD OF another struct)*, so `/events` and the blackboard translators rendered an entity's `Name` as a byte-buffer object — ⛔ **precisely the *"raw list of 64 byte values"* the mapper's own doc-comment says it exists to avoid.** ⇒ `EventSerializationHelperTests` ×2 were a **real defect**, not a stale assertion
- [x] **QA-008** · `RW-M` ✅ 🔴🔴 — **`DEBT-AIB-030`'s REAL root cause in `Hrot.SimHost.Tests`, and the ledger's hypothesis was FALSE.** ⛔ *"ids are assigned in registration order and parallelism makes that observable"* *(`Q52` §6.3 · `ST-026` · `AX-023`)* — 📐 measured **false**: `GetOrRegisterManaged` **requires** an explicit `[ComponentId]` and throws without one, so ids are **deterministic**. ⭐⭐⭐ **What parallelism makes observable is `ComponentTypeRegistry.Clear()`** — `BlueprintStateTranslatorTests` calls it in its constructor, this assembly has no `xunit.runner.json`, and the call wipes a PROCESS-GLOBAL dictionary out from under whatever concurrent test is between *"register"* and *"look up."* ⇒ the identity rotates and every victim passes under `--filter`. ⭐ Fixed by **isolation** *(a `DisableParallelization` collection + a source-scan rail so a future caller cannot join silently)* — ⛔ this hides no failure; it removes an unsynchronised mutation of shared state
- [x] **QA-009** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **the gizmo *"unregistered type"* sentinels were REGISTERABLE, so they got registered.** `SC_GZ004_2`/`SC_GZ022_2` assert that an unregistered component type throws, using sentinel structs carrying `[ComponentId(248)]`/`[ComponentId(249)]`; the registry is process-global and monotonic, so once anything registered them the throw could not happen. ⚠ **Both files already named the mechanism in a `STABILITY(Flaky)` comment and carried the TRAIT instead of the fix.** ⭐ Dropping the attribute makes the sentinel un-registerable **by any path** — the absence IS the invariant. Both traits removed with the defect *(`R-131`)*
- [x] **QA-010** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐⭐ — **an un-timestamped log line was silently DROPPED.** `LogArchiveExtractionService` tracked per-record age with `currentRecordPassesAge = false` and only set it on a parseable `[yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff]` prefix ⇒ a file with **no** timestamps archived **EMPTY**, and a real file lost its header lines. ⭐ Starting `true` also makes the age half agree with the severity half one method below, which documents itself as *"lines that cannot be parsed pass through by default (fail-safe)"* — ⛔ the two halves of one filter had opposite policies. ⚠ **My first hypothesis was wrong** *(the NLog-probe shadowing the caller's directory)* and is NOT in the diff: re-testing without it proved it was never load-bearing
- [x] **QA-011** · `RW-L` ✅ ⭐ — **`EntityDragGizmoTests` ×3 are STALE TESTS; production is right.** ⛔ EDG-001 drew against `new EntityRepository()` *(an empty world where the entity is not alive)*; EDG-002 grabbed at the ORIGIN and expected the entity to teleport onto the cursor, when `OnInteractionStarted` deliberately records `_dragOffset = position - grabPoint`; EDG-003 committed **without dragging**, and `OnCommit`'s `if (_isDragging)` guard is **correct** — without it every plain CLICK would move the entity. ⭐ A **new** rail pins the grab-offset contract so the next reader of *"expected 50, actual 60"* does not repeat the diagnosis. ⚠ Test-only: nothing here enters gizmo production *(the UI/CGF lane's neighbourhood)*

The assertion stays: it permanently removes one class of misdiagnosis. **Needs a batch that can carry a record/replay investigation**

## 🎮 Unreal parity reference

> **Why this table exists.** The user: *"we want to support most of what Unreal can, as this is a cheap
> source of 'is that a good approach' responses."* Unreal is the yardstick this programme already used
> for BP-71/BP-73/BP-75; this makes it explicit and checkable instead of recalled from memory.
>
> ⚠ **Use it as evidence, not authority.** Verify against the linked docs before a claim justifies a
> design — this programme has overturned ten audit claims and two architect statements. Two entries
> below were checked and came back *"we already have it"* (`Library` dispatch, implicit widening),
> which is exactly the failure mode to guard against.

### Authoring surface

| Unreal | Here | Item |
|---|---|---|
| Functions created from **My Blueprint → Functions +** | ✅ shipped (BP-24) | — |
| Inputs/Outputs edited in the **Details panel of the entry *or* result node**, or the My Blueprint item — **three** entry points | ❌ one place only, a separate **Graph Signature** window the designer never connects to the Return node in front of them | **BP-89** |
| Input params = data-**out** pins on the entry node; outputs = data-**in** pins on the return node | ✅ exactly our shape | — (BP-71/BP-73 got this right) |
| **Function-local variables** | ❌ `Graph` has no `LocalVariables` field | **BP-57** |
| **Collapse selection → Function / Macro** | ✅ **done** (Batch 33 core · Batch 34 sink, one undo entry, menu) | **BP-74** |
| Functions appear in the palette and can be **dragged** onto a graph | ❌ catalog never iterates `asset.Graphs` | **BP-75** |
| **Go to Definition** on a call node | ❌ gate tests demo kind-ids that never match | **BP-76** |
| **Event Graph** always exists, and more can be added | ❌ no "Graphs +"; a functions-only Instance asset has none | **BP-88** |
| Rename via **F2 / right-click**, everywhere | ❌ double-click only, no affordance, no hint — **third instance of this pattern** | **BP-90** |
| **Blueprint Function Library** — separate asset, callable project-wide | ⭐ `Dispatch: Library` **already exists end-to-end**; the editor just can't create one | **BP-92** |
| **Blueprint Macro Library** | 📐 designed ([Q25](Architect_Question_25_Macros.md)); asset-local macros first | **BP-79**…**BP-83** |
| Library functions callable with **no declaration** | ❌ hand-maintained `CallablePeers` per consumer | **BP-95** |

### Wiring and types

| Unreal | Here | Item |
|---|---|---|
| **Implicit widening** on the wire (`int`→`float`) | ⭐ **already works** — `Stage3_Normalize:275-292` auto-inserts a `CastNode` | — |
| **`Truncate`** node for the lossy direction (`float`→`int`) | ❌ `Single→Int32` absent from the coercion table ⇒ BP1501 with no remedy | **BP-96** |
| Wire-time feedback: autocast **tooltip**; incompatible ⇒ **icon + reason, refused** | ❌ **no link type-check anywhere in the editor** — every bad wire draws and fails at build | **BP-97** |
| Type picker offers only usable types | ❌ 8 of 15 offered types don't resolve; **no string type offered at all** though three are registered | **BP-87** |

| **Blueprint Interfaces** | Not raised by any user report; note it exists rather than building speculatively |
| Macro Library scoped by **parent class** | A good idea, but downstream of macros existing at all — revisit after BP-79…BP-83 |

## Confidence

**No unverified rows remain.** Every issue is hand-verified (**✔✔**) or spot-checked (**✔**), except
BP-53/BP-54 which are explicitly flagged **UNCLEAR**. Per-issue tags live in the detail file.

**Seven** "nothing exists" claims have now been overturned:

| # | Claim | Where it actually lived |
|---:|---|---|
| 1–4 | the predicate editing UI · Universal Breakpoints · C1-for-BTree · BP-46 | `FDP/`, not `Hrot/` |
| 5–6 | collapse-to-function (`BP-74`) · macros (`BP-78`) — the audit register had both filed **out of scope as absent** | `FDP/ExtDeps/NodeEdit/` |
| 7 | *"the macro expansion pass must write its own node cloning"* (`BP-81`) | **`Hrot/` all along** — `BlueprintClipboard.Rehydrate`, shipped by `BP-23a` in this very programme |

**Lessons.** (a) Absence claims must be checked across **both** trees — that is 1–6.
(b) ⚠ **#7 is the more uncomfortable one: the code was in `Hrot/`, and it was ours.** No cross-tree
rule would have caught it; the fix had shipped as `BP-23a` and was simply not recalled when scoping a
later item. Before writing "no prior art exists", grep the **done** rows of this tracker.
(c) #7 surfaced only because a link-validator false positive forced a re-read of the `BP-23a` row —
the second time in this programme that a *broken tool* found a real defect. Check the tool, but read
what it points at.
